generated_output.summary: CLI startup crashes with an unhandled ENOSPC error when Node.js `fs.watch` reaches the system inotify watch limit while monitoring the `~/.kimi-code` directory or configuration files.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: During CLI startup and initialization, the application sets up file system watchers using Node's `fs.watch` via dependencies (such as config/state watchers on `~/.kimi-code`). When the system limit for inotify watches is exhausted, Node's `fs.watch` synchronously or asynchronously throws an `ENOSPC` error which propagates unhandled to the process level, terminating execution.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect handleMainCommand initialization flow
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect handleMainCommand in apps/kimi-code/src/main.ts to locate where configuration and state directory file watchers are established via fs.watch.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect ensureInnerKaos setup in ACP server
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect ensureInnerKaos in packages/acp-adapter/src/server.ts to identify secondary file system watcher attachments prone to ENOSPC errors.

step_by_step_plan.title: Wrap fs.watch calls with error handlers for ENOSPC
step_by_step_plan.description: Add explicit .on('error', ...)` listeners or try/catch blocks around fs.watch invocations in main.ts and server.ts to catch ENOSPC exceptions, log a warning message, and degrade gracefully without crashing.

step_by_step_plan.title: Implement regression test and verify with test command
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a unit test that mocks fs.watch to emit an ENOSPC error upon initialization and verifies the application handles it gracefully without crashing, then run pnpm test.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Catching expected runtime exceptions (like filesystem limits) instead of allowing them to crash the application.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Ensures that minor environmental constraints do not bring down the entire CLI or development tool unexpectedly.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: File watcher setup needs `try/catch` or error event listeners around `fs.watch` calls to safely handle `ENOSPC` without terminating the process.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Node.js built-in API for monitoring changes to files and directories.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Developer tools use file watchers to auto-reload configuration or sync state, but OS limits can restrict the number of active watchers.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The crash specifically originates from Node's `fs.watch` failing when system limits are exceeded.

common_pitfalls: Catching errors too broadly and swallowing unexpected critical application startup failures.
Modifying global process uncaughtException handlers instead of robustly wrapping local filesystem initialization calls.
